title: mitigate hosted API GPU queue spikes via throttling + scale policy improvements
creator: Nina Patel
description: Post-incident follow-up for the hosted API GPU capacity exhaustion event on 2026-03-08 where sustained peak traffic caused request queues to build up, triggering broad throttling and elevated latencies across multiple regions. This ticket tracks the engineering plan to (1) add queue-aware scaling signals, (2) implement ingress-level backpressure and token-bucket throttling per route, (3) reserve emergency headroom for reserved customers, and (4) improve observability/alerts and runbooks so next incidents are contained with less customer impact. The work is deliberately scoped into short, testable milestones so we can deploy incremental mitigations within the same week.
root_cause: Autoscaler decision surface relied primarily on host-level GPU utilization and pod count. During the incident, requests with long decoding times accumulated in the frontend request queue faster than the GPU-based autoscaler could spin up compatible inference pods. This caused sustained queue growth, upstream retries, and cascading throttles. Additionally, there was no per-route token-bucket throttle or priority queueing to protect SLAs for dedicated customers.
timeline: 2026-03-08 03:12 UTC — first signs: queue depth spike on gpu-hosted-prod-us-west dashboard
2026-03-08 03:25 UTC — autoscaler attempted scale but new pods did not register fast enough (image pull delays in one AZ)
2026-03-08 03:40 UTC — platform enabled emergency burst capacity and fallback to smaller model variants for non-enterprise routes
2026-03-08 04:10 UTC — incident mitigated; traffic normalized by 04:40 after manual throttles and routes fallback
resolution_summary: Immediate mitigation combined temporary burst cluster allocation and coarse route-level throttles; incident declared resolved after traffic normalized. Permanent fixes prioritized: queue-aware scaling signal, ingress token-bucket implementation, model fallback policy automation, and improved alerting/runbook. Related PRs and dashboards created for verification.
action_items: A1: Implement queue-depth metric exporter in frontends (route-level, per-AZ) and wire to autoscaler feed — owner: Marco — estimate 3
A2: Add queue-aware autoscaling algorithm (scale when queue_depth/sec > X for 30s) and feature-flag rollout — owner: Priya Mehta — estimate 5
A3: Implement ingress token-bucket per-route throttling with burst allowance and priority tiers (enterprise/dedicated exempted) — owner: Marco — estimate 5
A4: Reserve 10% headroom capacity for hosted clusters during business-hours via reservation policy short-term — owner: infra-ops — estimate 2
A5: Automate fallback to quantized/smaller model variants when queue depth exceeds threshold for a route — owner: ML infra — estimate 4
A6: Add alerts for 1) sustained queue depth > 2500 reqs for 5m, 2) queued request latency p99 > 6s, and 3) image-pull failure rate > 1% during scale-up — owner: Observability — estimate 1
A7: Update runbook with step-by-step mitigation (enable burst clusters, apply route-throttle, trigger model-fallback) and schedule on-call training — owner: SRE — estimate 1
A8: End-to-end test harness: synthetic traffic generator and chaos tests (AZ image-pull slowdowns) — owner: QA — estimate 3
acceptance_criteria: AC1: New queue-depth metric is emitted per-route and visible in Grafana with correct timestamps
AC2: Autoscaler responds to queue-depth signal and reduces average queue depth by >= 60% under the same synthetic load in staging
AC3: Token-bucket throttling enforces configured burst and sustained rate and prevents cross-route SLA bleed in experiments
AC4: Runbook updated and on-call sim completed with playbook verifying mitigations within 15 minutes
AC5: No functional regression in request correctness or auth; load tests in staging pass with <1% error rate
